root_cause: RFC-029 D7 table segmentation (_segment_table_nodes) causes node explosion from 502→~2042 nodes; new low_content_density gate (threshold 500 chars/node) rejects the resulting tree. Both features introduced in commit 08b6eea (RFC-029 implementation).
mechanism: 1. Tree builder (md_to_tree) produces 502-node tree with ~110k chars (same as Run 12). 2. _segment_table_nodes examines nodes for pipe-tables with >=5 rows and >2000 chars. 3. Each qualifying node is split into child nodes (one per table block + inter-table prose). 4. For a hierarchical legal document with multiple embedded tables, this explodes the tree to ~2000+ nodes. 5. validate_tree checks total_nodes >= 200 && chars_per_node < 500 — both conditions met. 6. Tree is rejected with low_content_density ERROR.
why_run_12_passed: RFC-029 code was committed AFTER Run 12 (commit 08b6eea). Run 12 did not have _segment_table_nodes or low_content_density gate.
why_not_repair_docling_tables: _repair_docling_tables strips GFM whitespace (~10% reduction), applied before tree building. This affects markdown char count, not node count. The 4x node explosion is the only mechanism for 54.3 chars/node.
fix_strategy: Lower threshold to ~200 chars/node or exclude child nodes from density check. Add low_content_density to recovery paths in client.py.
